text:
maria: FYI nightly eval run just finished — product-faqs promptset EM down ~42% vs baseline. A lot of accepted answers are missing the leading 'Q:' marker or have weird invisible chars in the outputs.
aj: Seen. Which model/variant shows the drop? new-int8 only or fp16 too?
kai: Any failing samples we can eyeball?
maria: It's across new-int8-v2 and fp16-run (so not a quant-only perf bug). Pasting one failed pair we observed (copied verbatim):

Sample ID: 48231
Prompt (as stored): "Q:\u200bWhat is your refund policy?
Please explain the steps."
Model output: "We refund within 30 days..." (but EM mismatch because tokenizer split Q: into separate token sequence)

maria: Note the '\u200b' in the stored prompt (that's U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE). I suspect copy/paste from a Google Doc introduced invisible chars into the template.
eval-bot: nightly-metrics: product-faqs EM baseline=0.78 -> new=0.45; failed_examples=412/1000; top-token-diff includes unexpected token id 831 (occurs at prompt boundaries).
samir: Can you grep for U+200B across the promptset dir? quick check would rule out harness vs model.
maria: Ran a quick search: `grep -nP '\x{200B}' promptsets/product-faqs/templates/* || true` -> matches: `promptsets/product-faqs/templates/template_03.txt:1:Q:\u200bWhat is your refund policy?` (commit 5c4b3a). Looks like the template file contains literal ZWSP.
kai: That explains why tokenization counts changed for that prompt. Normal sanitizer removed trailing whitespace but didn't strip invisible Unicode control chars (category Cf). Tokenizer then produced an extra subtoken boundary and attention alignment shifted — downstream outputs differ.
aj: So root cause hypothesis: invisible ZERO-WIDTH-SPACE introduced via copy/paste into template + evaluation harness didn't canonicalize prompts -> tokenization mismatch -> quality regression detectable by nightly eval; manifest on multiple variants because it's an input issue.
maria: Short-term mitigation: revert the commit that added the contaminated template (revert promptsets/product-faqs@5c4b3a) and re-run nightly to confirm EM recovers.
samir: Mid-term actions I'm proposing: 1) add prompt canonicalizer that strips Unicode invisible chars (categories Cf, e.g., U+200B/U+200C etc.) and performs NFKC normalization before tokenization; 2) add a pre-commit hook that scans promptset files for disallowed codepoints; 3) add a nightly gating check: if canonicalized token_count differs from raw token_count by >1 for any prompt, fail the eval and alert; 4) run a targeted canary: sanitize prompts and run 5% of nightly with sanitized prompt pipeline to compare diffs.
kai: Also add a unit test that iterates all prompt templates and asserts no control/invisible chars are present. Add an eslint-like linter for promptsets.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: promptsets/product-faqs reverted 5c4b3a -> 5c4b39 by @maria at 1738999060
maria: Thanks @ops-bot. I'll open the sanitizer PR and the pre-commit hook PR now. @aj can you add alerting for EM drops >10% on product-faqs and a secondary alert if token-count-delta > 2?
aj: Yep, adding alert rule to monitoring (prod-faqs.EM.alert threshold=10%) and a waveform check for token-count drift.
samir: PRs: (#1224) promptset-sanitizer, (#1225) pre-commit.lint for promptsets. ETA EOD for both. I'll also add a small script to re-scan all historical promptsets and create a csv of files with suspicious codepoints.
maria: Good. After revert + PRs, plan: re-run nightly, then run 1k-sanity canary against new-int8-v2 with sanitized prompts. If green, continue with rollout; if not, escalate to model team.
kai: Minor follow-up: add note in onboarding docs about "avoid direct Google Doc copy/paste into templates" and prefer our prompt editor or paste-then-canonicalize flow.
maria: Agreed. Also scheduling a short retro tomorrow to discuss better prompt hygiene and harness hardening. Tagging @aj @samir. :thumbsup:
aj: I'll monitor the canary and alert. :eyes:
samir: running the historical scan now, will post link when done.
maria: Thanks all — closing thread once canary is green and PRs merged.
